text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- ASEAN wins crucial support from big powers for initiative to restore political stability in Cambodia.
- Cambodia's ousted First Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh expells his slated replacement from royalist Funcinpec party following Cambodia's "coup d'etat".
- Cough-and-cold-only family doctor fading away in Singapore. Emerging figure in neighbourhood clinics is "minor" surgeon who can remove lumps and bumps and even do simple biopsy.

- Scientist who led team that produced Dolly the sheep, world's first clone of adult animal, said in interview that clones are often born abnormally large and die soon after, putting paid to any commercial potential for project.
- Singapore exports of services set to hit Singapore $50 billion mark this year, having grown by nearly 10 percent annually in 1990s.
- George Soros has two qualities which make him nightmare for certain governments: He has pretensions of being one-man defender of democracy and has financial clout of small country.

- Resale transactions for most types of HDB flats have been hard hit by government moves in April and May to tighten financing and shorten HDB queue, with data from property research firm Info-Tools showing impact was almost immediate.

- Real estate broker Simon Cheong will receive cool S$15 million in commissions for S$359 million sale of Forum, or four times more than standard one percent brokerage for property deals in Singapore.
- Japanese purchases of US and European bonds and equities slowed down considerably in past month because of worries about currency losses, say dealers and analysts.
- Allgreen Properties' impending listing looks set to be biggest local-dollar debut on market in last few years in terms of asset base.
- Robert Kuok, hailed by Forbes magazine as world's shrewdest businessman, is always looking for people smarter than himself to go into joint ventures.
